title: The Enron Scandal Explained: Why Its CEO Got 24 Years
summary:
The Enron scandal explained from the court record: how Enron executive Jeffrey Skilling told investors "Let me repeat that," sold 500,000 shares the day markets reopened after 9/11, and was convicted of conspiracy, securities fraud and insider trading in Houston in 2006.
Built from the Fifth Circuit's opinion, the grand jury's superseding indictment, the trial docket, the Justice Department's own releases and the Supreme Court's 2010 ruling in Skilling v. United States — including how the 24-year sentence became 14.
docs_note: Documents shown are U.S. court records and U.S. Department of Justice filings (public domain).
